defects.severity: high (write through a C-valid NULL/zero-length buffer; the authority has the same UB and it is not reproduced)
defects.class: out-of-contract terminator write on the zero-length gets path (AGENTS.md sections 17 and 21.1)
defects.description: mem_gets wrote `*buf = 0` whenever the computed j was <= 0. BIO_gets admits a buffer valid for `size` bytes, and for `size == 0` a NULL or zero-length buffer satisfies that contract, so `BIO_gets(b, NULL, 0)` dereferenced NULL. The authority's bss_mem.c:357-360 has the same defect.
defects.fix: Write the terminator only when `size > 0` (where j <= 0 means size == 1) and `buf` is non-NULL; the answer stays the authority's 0. The cap is also computed with saturating_sub so INT_MIN cannot overflow the `size - 1` expression. Control: runtime::bio::bss_mem::tests::a_zero_length_gets_does_not_write_through_a_null_buffer.
defects.divergence: Deliberate: for size 0 the buffer is left untouched instead of writing a byte the caller has no writable extent for. Return value and all size > 0 behaviour are unchanged.

defects.severity: medium (fallible arithmetic; release behaviour unchanged, debug builds could panic)
defects.class: unchecked length sum on an allocation/growth path (AGENTS.md section 3)
defects.description: mem_write computed `blen + inl as usize` without a checked add. A negative `inl` reaches the growth as an enormous size_t (the authority's modular arithmetic) and fails there; on Rust debug builds the addition panics instead, relying on a panic boundary rather than translating to the authority's failure.
defects.fix: Use checked_add and return the authority's -1 (`ret`) on overflow; every unallocatable enormous length already fails BUF_MEM_grow_clean, so the observable refusal is the same.
defects.divergence: None for conforming input; the refusal path is now explicit rather than a wrapped allocation request.

defects.class: documented precondition did not establish out-parameter validity (AGENTS.md sections 7 and 21)
defects.description: The # Safety section for EVP_PKEY_CTX_get_dh_kdf_outlen described `plen` as "NULL or a live int the callee writes", while a 1 return executes `*plen = len as c_int`; a caller following the contract could pass NULL and cause UB.
defects.fix: State that `plen` is a live, writable int written on a 1 return.
